parsed.answer: The claim is supported: an autoimmune disease-associated IL2RA haplotype correlated with diminished IL-2 responsiveness (reduced STAT5a phosphorylation) in Ag-experienced CD4+ T cells, lower FOXP3 expression in Tregs, and reduced suppressive capacity, in studies using healthy human subjects to avoid disease confounds. Corroborating mouse evidence shows that reduced IL-2 production via Idd3/Il2 susceptibility alleles correlates with reduced CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cell function. Treg dysfunction is thus linked to IL-2/IL-2 signaling defects and to Type 1 Diabetes-associated variants.
